title: Sign Restrictions and Supply-demand Decompositions of Inflation - Replication Spec
hypothesis: Sign restrictions on slopes alone are largely uninformative about historical decompositions of US inflation in aggregate and most PCE categories; wide robust identified sets span 0.2-7.3 of 7.7pp at US 2022:Q2 peak and around 0-6.8 of 7.9pp at EA 2022:Q4 peak with low rho~0.23 [0.13,0.33]; sharp only when |rho| large and realised error aligns e.g. food farms rho=-0.98 with 23.9-25.1 of 28.4% in Mar2022; joint hypothesis lower=0 upper=0.99 vs uniform 0.5, so conclusions depend on auxiliary prior assumptions.
data_sources: Bureau of Economic Analysis National Accounts Underlying Detail Tables for PCE categories (price and real expenditure); FRED/Giannone-Primiceri replication data for US log CPI and log real GDP 1997:Q1-2019:Q4 and euro HICP.
sample: Main aggregate decomposition: 4-lag Bayesian VAR in log CPI and log real GDP estimated on 1997:Q1-2019:Q4, post-2019 historical decompositions of year-ended inflation given information to 2019:Q4. Disaggregated decomposition: OLS 12-lag VAR in monthly PCE inflation and real expenditure growth for 136 PCE categories estimated on 1988:M1-2023:M9. Trivariate illustration: simulated sample of 100 one-step forecast errors with rho_{12} approx -1. Larger 3-variable SVARs: 17 post-2019 quarters (2020:Q1-...). N for estimation windows in calendar time is given by periods, N counts printed only for n_PCE_categories_total =136, n_trivariate_simulation_draws=100, dimension_d_3var_post2019_periods=17; other N not printed as integer.
method: 1. Aggregate: estimate 4-lag VAR of (p_t=log CPI, q_t=log real GDP) on 1997:Q1-2019:Q4 with Minnesota + sum-of-coefficients prior per Giannone-Lenza-Primiceri. Draw phi posterior.

2. At each phi draw compute rho = sigma21/sqrt(sigma21^2+sigma22^2), IS_theta(phi) = [arctan(sigma22/sigma21),0] if rho<0 else [-pi/2, arctan(-sigma21/sigma22)] and A0^{-1}(theta). Sign restrictions A0^{-1}=[+,+;- ,+] equivalent to A0=[+,-;+,+].

3. Historical decomposition H_{t,t+h}(theta,phi,{u}) = [cos theta sin theta] Omega_h(phi,{u}) [cos theta; sin theta] with Omega_h = sum_{l=0}^h c_{1l}(phi)(Sigma_tr^{-1} u_{t+h-l})', c_{1h}'=e1' C_h Sigma_tr, Ch recursion.

4. Year-ended inflation pi_t^{(ye)}=p_t-p_{t-4} (quarterly) or sum_{l=0}^{11} pi_{t-l} (monthly). Decompose as H_{t,t+h}-H_{t,t+h-4} (h>=4) or sum_{h=0}^{11} H_{1,t-h} via Omega_tilde = Omega_h - Omega_{h-4} or sum Omega_{t-h}. End points L_{t,t+h},U_{t,t+h} = min/max_{theta in IS_theta} H(theta) obtained by evaluating at two endpoints of IS_theta and at <=2 normalized eigenvectors of S_h=(Omega_h+Omega_h')/2 that satisfy sign normalization and lie in IS_theta.

5. Aggregate baseline: 10,000 draws of phi, 10 draws of theta uniform over IS_theta(phi) at each phi =100,000 draws of (phi,theta); report posterior mean under uniform. Robust Bayes: class of conditional priors on IS_theta(phi); set of posterior means approx = posterior mean of L and U; 68% robust credible interval = tau/2 quantile of L and 1-tau/2 quantile of U.

6. Joint hypothesis: H = union_{t in 2021:Q2-2022:Q2} {tilde H_t <= 0.5 FE_t} where tilde H_t = supply contribution to year-ended forecast error, FE_t= forecast error; posterior lower/upper probabilities approximated with 10,000 theta draws per phi uniform over IS_theta.

7. Disaggregated: for each of 136 categories OLS 12-lag VAR on 1988:M1-2023:M9 in (monthly PCE inflation in log differences, real expenditure growth); compute IS_{H} for sum_{h=0}^{11} H_{1,t-h} via Omega_tilde = sum_{h=0}^{11} Omega_{t-h}.

8. Trivariate illustration DGP with rho12 approx -1, rho13 small positive, rho23 small negative; simulate 100 forecast errors; approximate IS_{H_{t,t}} by min/max over ~55,000 uniform Q draws from identified set via Rubio-Ramirez-Waggoner-Zha; 3-variable GP24 models approximate endpoints with 10,000 uniform Q draws, K=10,494 per Montiel-Olea-Nesbit Thm3 for d=17, epsilon=delta=0.01.
